title: Cascade Failure Propagation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Compelling and critical: multi-agent AI systems are increasingly common, and understanding whether diversity reduces cascade failure is directly actionable for system designers. Tests the causal chain from shared blind spots to coordinated failure.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Multi-agent pipeline construction requires intermediate programming. Identifying shared blind spots from single-model testing and then tracing propagation adds experimental design complexity. Manageable with guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: construct 3-5 model pipelines, inject known blind spots, measure propagation in homogeneous vs. diverse pipelines. Well-defined comparison experiment achievable in 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: This is substantially addressed by recent work. 'Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?' (arXiv:2503.13657, 2025) provides a comprehensive failure taxonomy (MAST) with 1600+ annotated traces across 7 MAS frameworks, identifying cascade failures and error propagation as key failure modes. 'Where LLM Agents Fail and How They Can Learn From Failures' (arXiv:2509.25370, 2025) identifies error propagation as a key bottleneck. Critically, the homogeneous vs. heterogeneous comparison is partially addressed: research shows Anthropic models benefit from heterogeneous mixing and that monoculture collapse occurs when agents share correlated vulnerabilities. The specific contribution of injecting known blind spots and measuring propagation remains partially novel, but the core question is substantially addressed.
